site.name: Connaught Place
site.survey: Lutyens' bazaar cordon reconstruction: ring and radial turning counts from the CP area traffic study, 12-h weekday; ring radii measured on the satellite capture (Outer Circle ~95 m, Inner Circle ~42 m)
site.summary: One-way Outer and Inner Circles pierced by six radial corridors. Every radial is metered twice - once at its Outer Circle entry and again where the circulating band penetrates the Inner Circle - so a plaza crossing costs a lap of each band and almost every movement corners. That makes this the site where the curvature term a_curve dominates: cars slow through the 42 m Inner Circle and re-accelerate on the exit, while inner trips that must cross both bands and the radial exits form queues continuously rather than in bands.

imagery.bearing_note: the concentric rings are centred on this pixel

signals.name: Circle crossings
signals.notes: One stage pair per radial: A holds the Outer Circle mouths while the radial crosses it, B holds the Inner Circle mouths while the chord crosses the plaza - the circulating bands themselves are never held

scenarios.name: Vip movement: Barakhamba closed
scenarios.note: The ENE radial is shut; its traffic creeps round the Outer Circle instead and the ring queues back onto the crossings.

scenarios.name: Ring flood (Inner Circle over-supplied)
scenarios.note: Every radial pushes harder than the Inner Circle can discharge - watch the standstill alert trip inside the plaza.

scenarios.name: Curvature study (20 km/h through the plaza)
scenarios.note: Limits cut on both circles to isolate the a_curve term's platoon-shockwave effect on the ring.
